beats.text: Say the word spoon. Again. Again. Again.
Spoon. Spoon. Spoon. Spoon. Spoon. Spoon.
At some point, it stops sounding like a word.
It's called semantic satiation. A psychologist named it in nineteen sixty-two.
Repeat a word enough and the link to its meaning gets tired. Like a muscle.
Your brain isn't glitching. It's just tired of spoon.

sources: Jakobovits (James) (1962). Effects of repeated stimulation on cognitive aspects of behavior. Doctoral dissertation, McGill University (term 'semantic satiation').

Severance & Washburn (1907). The loss of associative power in words after long fixation. American Journal of Psychology 18. Mechanism (reactive inhibition) is a proposed explanation. Via Wikipedia 'Semantic satiation'.
